newsitem.title: USA: Zenith Q1 helped by higher sales, lower cost.
newsitem.headline: Zenith Q1 helped by higher sales, lower cost.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp said Tuesday the narrowing of its first quarter net loss compared with a year ago reflected higher sales and lower costs.
Earlier, Zenith reported a first quarter net loss of $25.2 million or $0.38 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $35.3 million or $0.56 a share.

The improved results reflect the "combined effect of higher sales and lower costs resulting from the aggressive turnaround plan being implemented by Zenith's new management team," Peter Willmott, president, said in a statement.
He added that cost controls offset start-up problems associated with new color picture tube production equipment at the company's Melrose Park, Ill., plant.

Zenith's color television sales to U.S. dealers were up sharply in the quarter, despite the picture tube availability problems, the company said. It added the Zenith brand increased its domestic color TV market share in the quarter, particularly in key large-screen categories.
Zenith's sales of video cassette recorders (VCRs) and color picture tubes sold to other manufacturers also increased.
Sales of Network Systems products -- such as set-top boxes and cable modems sold primarily to the cable TV industry -- declined from the first quarter of 1996.
"While the short term continues to be difficult, we are optimistic about the prospects for future revenue growth and profit improvement," Willmott said.

He said investments in Zenith's U.S. and Mexican factories are expected to boost productivity and efficiency this year. In addition, Zenith is focusing on higher-margin home theater TV systems, supported by the second-half 1997 launch of the company's first national advertising campaign in five years.
The company also plans to begin shipments in 1997 of high-resolution computer display tubes to computer monitor manufacturers, as well as new digital set-top boxes to telecommunications companies.
In early April, Zenith obtained new financing commitments that will improve the company's financial flexibility and support its turnaround strategy.

Zenith's largest shareholder is LG Electronics Inc which, together with its affiliate LG Semicon, currently owns 55 percent of the company's outstanding shares. Options, when exercised, would increase LG's interest to 57.5 percent.
